correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty equivalence frame, finite Boolean duality makes every powerset Boolean endomorphism the inverse image of a unique set map. The modal law is equivalent to the equality of successor images and thus to independent surjections from each source cluster to a target cluster. Exactly a_j! S(a_i,a_j) such local maps exist. Inclusion-exclusion over the set of occupied target clusters gives the unrestricted rank polynomial; idempotence forces the complete image to be fixed pointwise and gives the anchor-product formula. A minimum-size source cluster cannot surject onto anything larger, while an anchored minimum-size cluster accepts surjections from every omitted cluster. This proves necessity and sufficiency of the support criterion, equality of unrestricted and idempotent rank sets, and the exact image-type count. The universal proof is independent of finite computations. The standalone checker has passed 16 complete small-frame sweeps with 197086 function tables and 10874 direct modal subset equations.

originality.rationale: The result is assessed as the combined unequal-cluster-size idempotent and unrestricted image-rank classification, the minimum-cluster retraction-support obstruction, and equality of rank supports. Classical S5 cluster semantics, Boolean duality, surjection/Stirling numbers, and ordinary finite-transformation-monoid identities are expressly excluded from the priority claim. The accessible primary article concerns completeness and Baire algebras rather than these enumerations; two more directly related older articles concern endomorphism-monoid reconstruction and counts of subalgebras, respectively. Full-text limits of those older works are explicitly named and prevent a claim of definitive priority, but the available statements do not imply the complete rank-refined classification.

value.rationale: For finite equivalence frames, the natural question of how modal structure restricts Boolean retractions has a sharp nontrivial solution: every allowed image support must contain a minimum-size equivalence class and this condition suffices. The entire image-cardinality spectrum of arbitrary maps equals that of idempotent maps, but their exact coefficients are different and are computed by distinct formulas. The theorem gives a complete motivated heterogeneous-size classification, the exact number of attainable dual retraction supports, and the number of distinct modal-algebra image isomorphism types, rather than a narrow ad hoc small example. It distinguishes the modal situation from unrestricted Boolean transformations and is reproducible by direct finite tests.
